_comment: Per-calculator page metadata. One entry per page; the card id ties it to
PM_DATA, and `content` names the prose file beside this one.
title       — under ~60 characters, or Google truncates it in results.
description — 140-160 characters. It is the sales pitch in the result list.
h1          — the on-page heading. May differ from the title tag.
related     — card ids to link to at the foot of the page.
Everything else about the page (the calculator, its formula, its charts)
comes from PM_DATA, so it can never drift out of step with the desk.

URLs end in .html because that is how Apache serves the file. Extensionless URLs (/earned-value-analysis) would need one RewriteRule, guarded inside <IfModule mod_rewrite.c> like every other directive in .htaccess. Worth doing before there are many pages and links to them, not after.

pages.title: Earned Value Analysis — CPI, SPI, EAC Calculator
pages.description: Work through earned value with real numbers: CPI, SPI, EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI computed live, which EAC formula to use, and where SPI stops telling the truth.
pages.h1: Earned value analysis, worked through end to end
pages.lede: Enter four numbers and every earned-value metric updates live. Below the calculator: a full worked example, the four EAC formulas and when each one is right, and the mistakes that survive into real project reporting.
